title: YOUR GUILT IS TAKEN AWAY.
paragraphs: YOUR GUILT IS TAKEN AWAY.
Let that line slow you down for a second.

Not minimized.
Not explained away.
Not buried under religious performance.
Taken. Away.
That’s the scandal Isaiah experienced the moment heaven touched his life.
And it started with terror.
Isaiah did not walk into a cozy worship service.
He stepped into a collision with holiness.
“The Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and the train of his robe filled the temple.” (Isaiah 6:1)
Seraphim hovered above Him like living flames.

Six wings.
Faces covered.
Feet covered.
Even sinless beings shielded themselves from the blazing purity of God.
And they cried out with thunder in their voices:
“Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts.”
Not loving, loving, loving.
Not merciful, merciful, merciful.
Holy.
The foundations of the temple shook.
Smoke flooded the room.
And in that moment, Isaiah stopped comparing himself to other people.
Because when you see God clearly…
You finally see yourself honestly.
Isaiah didn’t say:
“I’m doing my best.”
“I’m not that bad.”
“I’m better than most.”
No.
The prophet collapsed under the weight of truth.

“Woe is me! For I am undone.”
(Isaiah 6:5)
The Hebrew word means destroyed… unraveled… ruined.
Isaiah realized something devastating:
You can be religious and still be unclean.
He confessed:
“I am a man of unclean lips.”
Why lips?
Because lips reveal the heart.

The lies.
The gossip.
The pride.
The anger.
The hidden poison in words we thought nobody noticed.
And suddenly Isaiah realized:

The mouth meant to speak for God
…had been stained by sin.
Sound familiar?
Some of us know that feeling.
The moment when the Holy Spirit pulls back the curtain.

And the secret you hid.
The words you spoke.
The compromise you justified.
All of it suddenly stands under the light of God.
That moment feels terrifying.
But watch what happens next.
Because God did not destroy Isaiah.
He cleansed him.
One of the seraphim flew to the altar.
In his hand was a burning coal.
Fire from the place of sacrifice.
The angel touched Isaiah’s lips.
Imagine that moment.

Heat.
Shock.
Pain.
Not to punish him.
But to purify him.
And heaven declared something Isaiah could never declare over himself:

“Your guilt is taken away, and your sin atoned for.”
(Isaiah 6:7)
Did you see it?
Isaiah confessed his sin.
But God removed it.
Isaiah acknowledged the stain.
But God performed the cleansing.
Religion tells you:
“Fix yourself first.”
The Gospel says:
“Come broken. Jesus will cleanse you.”
That coal from the altar was not random.
It pointed forward.
Forward to a hill outside Jerusalem.
Forward to wood, nails, and blood.
Forward to Jesus Christ.
Because one day, the true altar would be the cross.
And the fire of God’s justice would not fall on us.
It would fall on Him.

Jesus carried our guilt.
Jesus bore our shame.
Jesus paid our debt.
So that heaven could say over sinners like you and me:
“Your guilt is taken away.”
Not because we improved ourselves.
But because Christ gave Himself.
And here’s the part many people miss.
The cleansing came before the calling.
Right after Isaiah was purified, he heard the voice of the Lord:
“Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?” (Isaiah 6:8)
Isaiah didn’t hesitate.
Not because he was perfect.
But because he had been forgiven.
He said:
“Here am I. Send me.”
God does not send flawless people.
He sends forgiven people.
People who remember what it felt like when grace touched their life.
People who know what it means to have guilt lifted off their chest.

People who once said, “Woe is me,”
but now say, “Use me.”
So let me ask you something honest.
What guilt are you carrying right now?

The secret sin?
The words you wish you could take back?
The failure nobody knows about?
You might feel like Isaiah:

Undone.
Exposed.
Unworthy.
But the message of the Gospel is this:
Grace still touches lips.
Not with a burning coal now…
But with the cleansing power of the cross.
Jesus did not come to shame sinners.
He came to save them.
And when His grace touches your life, heaven declares something the enemy hates hearing:
“Your guilt is taken away.”
Not postponed.
Not probation.
Gone.
Pause.
Pray.
Tell Jesus the truth about your life.
Because the same God who cleansed Isaiah is still cleansing sinners today.
And the moment grace touches your life…
Everything changes.

Your past loses its chains.
Your shame loses its voice.
Your future gets rewritten.
Because that’s what Jesus does.
He turns burning conviction into blazing redemption.
And suddenly the words that once condemned you become the testimony that frees others.
🔥 “Grace touched my life.”
Because someone you know needs to hear this today:
Your guilt is taken away.
